full_judgment:
7. Facts relevant for the purpose of disposal of the Rules, in brief, are that on 19-3-1997 a notice was issued under section 3 of the Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Property Ordinance, 1982 hereinafter called the Ordinance, for acquiring lands to establish Korean Export Processing Zones (KEPZ) in LA Case No. 12/1996-97; for acquisition of about 2,600 acres of land. Thereafter, on 24-7-1997 the Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong-respondent No. 2 prepared a report under section 4(3) of the said Ordinance and the same was placed before the Government for final decision. The petitioners filed objection on 7-4-1997, under section 4 of the Ordinance and after hearing both sides, i.e. the petitioners and the respondents, the Government decided to acquire a total area of 2527.76573 acres of land including the land of the petitioner in the Plot No. 11, BS Khatian No. 663 comprising 5.40 acres. Compensation was prepared and the notices were issued under section 7 on 8-7-1999 and 11-7-1999 respectively. Thereafter, the petitioner filed Writ Petition No. 2949 of 1999 challenging the decision of acquisition under section 5 of the Ordinance as well as the two compensation notices dated 8-7-1999 and 11-7-1999. The Hon'ble High Court Division on 19-1-2000 without issuing a Rule disposed of the aforesaid Writ petition with some directions to consider the value of the land and also value of the trees and structures as well as the loss incurred by the petitioner including Machinery, Bank loans etc. The petitioner challenged these directions before the Appellate Division filing Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal being No. 266 of 2000 and the respondent No. 1 and 4 also filed two Leave Petitions being No. 213 of 2000 and 214 of 2000. After hearing those Leave Petitions the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court disposed of those petitions directing the respondents to assess the compensation in accordance with law observing the formalities mentioned in section 8 of the Ordinance by judgment dated 18-5-2000. Thereafter, the Local Government and Engineering Department (LGED) after assessment, gave its report as to the compensation of the structures on the BS Khatian No. 663, Dag No. 11 which is owned by the petitioner. On 25-2-2001 the Land Acquisition Officer-respondent No. 3 after preparing the supplementary compensation served a notice to the respondent No. 4-Korean Export Processing Zone (KEPZ) to deposit compensation money. But the respondent No. 4 the KEPZ without depositing money made some representations to the Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong on 4-3-2001, 19-3-2001, 29-3-2001 and 27-8-2001 to reconsider the amount of the amount of the demand note made by the respondent No. 3. 

 24. We have gone through the Writ Petition along with the annexures, numbers of affidavits-in-opposition and supplementary affidavits and the annexures thereto and the relevant laws. We have also considered the submissions of the learned advocates of the petitioners and the respondents. It appears that notice under section 3 of Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Property Ordinance 1982 was published on 19-3-1997 for the land measuring an area of 7.56 acres under BS Dag No.11, Khatian No. 663 of Mouza: Bandar, IL No. 30, PS Bandar, District; Chittagong to establish KEPZ . After observing all formalities hearing the objections, the Government finally decided to acquire the land in the aforesaid Dag along with other land. Thereafter, asses-sing the compensation Government asked the KEPZ to pay Taka 64,20,16,717.80 as compensation of the acquired land. KEPZ challenged the said demand note by filing Writ Petition No. 1928 of 1999 but ultimately as per Court's decision KEPZ paid the amount demanded. On 8-7-1999, the Government served notice upon the respondent No. 4 under section 7 of the Ordinance for compensation for trees standing Dag No.11, Khatian no. 663, Mouza Bandar and on 11-7-99 served another notice for compensation for Dag No. 256, 257 and 239 of Mouza Badalpura, Writ Petitioner No. 1 challenged the notices dated 8-7-1999 and 11-7-1999 issued by the respondent No.3 upon the respondent No. 4 by filing Writ Petition No. 2949 of 1999 and by this Writ Petition the petitioner also challenged the decision taken by the Government under section 5 of the ordinance. On 19-1-2000 the High Court Division of Hon'ble Supreme Court disposed of the above mentioned Writ Petition with some directions to assess the compensation. Thereafter, the petitioner and the respondent No.4 preferred appeal against the judgment passed in Writ Petition No.2949 of 1999 by filing Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 266, 213 and 214 of 2000 respectively. The petitioner ultimately did not press its Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 266 of 2000. After hearing all the Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal, the Appellate Division disposed of Civil Petition No.213 and 214 of 2000 expunging the observation made by the High Court Division and directing the Government to assess compensation in accordance with law complying the provision laid down in the section 8 of the Ordinance. On 18-1-2001 the Local Government and Engineering Department gave its report as to estimation of structures of BS Khatian No. 663 BS Dag No. 11 and, thereafter, on 25-2-2001 Land Acquisition Officer asked the KEPZ to deposit Taka 4,61,41,184.40 vide annexure-H under section 7 (3) of the Ordinance as supplementary compensation. Against the said demand note the KEPZ, respondent No. 4 on 4-3-2001, 19-3-2001, 29-3-2001 and 27-8-2001 gave representation to the Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong to reconsider the supplementary demand note thereon. On getting several representations from the respondent No. 3, the LA officer asked the petitioner to remain present on 27-12-2001 at the site of Dag No. 11, Bandar Mouza for further survey. The order was challenged by the petitioner before this Court and this Court vide its order asked the petitioner and all others to complete the reassessment within two months and asked the petitioner to place his claim within this period to the Government. It further appears that after reassessment, the respondent No. 3 asked the respondent no.4 to deposit Taka 52,88,487.33 within 60 days revising its previous assessment of Taka 4,61,41,184.40. It also appears that the respondents after getting the notice under section 7 (3) of the Ordinance on 25-2-2001 without depositing the previously assessed compensation money to the Government, approached the Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong to reconsider the assessment. 

 27. Since the provision section 12(1) was totally ignored in passing the order in Writ Petition No.7001 of 2001, we are of the view that the judgment and order was passed in the said Writ Petition per incuriam and it had no binding effect upon any Court or any Executive. Since the compensation assessed earlier was not deposited within the stipulated period of 60 days we are of the view that the LA proceeding so far as relates to petitioner's property in Dag No. 11, BS khatian No. 663, Bandar Mouza, District-Chittagong stood abated automatically. 

 29. Although in our view the proceeding in LA Case No. 12/96-97 has been abated but nevertheless it cannot be said that further proceeding of new LA Case cannot be started. We have already seen the Sketch Map placed before us by the petitioner. If it is necessary for the purpose of the project to acquire further land, the Government is not precluded to do so, observing all legal formalities. Even the plot in question, i.e. Dag No. 11 BS Khatian No. 663 can also be acquired by the Government observing all formalities, paying proper compensation in accordance with law.
